NJ-2026-S4128.title: Requires county college to notify graduating high school students of acceptance into local county college.

actions.text: Received in the Assembly, Referred to Assembly Higher Education Committee
Passed by the Senate (39-0)
Reported from Senate Committee, 2nd Reading
Introduced in the Senate, Referred to Senate Higher Education Committee

NJ-2026-S4128.aiSummary: The bill would require each county college to send acceptance letters to local graduating 12th grade students who live in the county and attend public or nonpublic school. The letter would need to explain how to accept the offer, enroll, register for classes, and get financial aid and student support help. It would also require county college leaders to make guidelines for finding these students and to give a yearly report on the program.

NJ-2026-ACR160.title: Mandates disclosures for State budget resolutions regarding campaign contributions received by resolution sponsors from intended recipients of funds and the organizational classification of the intended recipients.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly State and Local Government Committee

NJ-2026-ACR160.aiSummary: This resolution would change New Jersey budget rules to require more disclosure from lawmakers who file budget resolutions. They would have to say what kind of group would get the money, such as a government, for-profit, or nonprofit group, and note if they or close family have ties to that group or got campaign money from its owners, officers, or board members in the past 36 months. It would affect sponsors of budget resolutions and the public record for state budget items.

NJ-2026-A5738.title: Revises "Fair Price Protection Act."

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Consumer Affairs Committee

NJ-2026-A5738.aiSummary: The bill would revise New Jersey’s Fair Price Protection Act, which deals with how prices are set for groceries and other food. It would let personal data used for pricing also be used for food safety notices, recall notices, and inventory forecasts, and it would allow some price changes more than once in a day for certain reasons like fixing errors or managing stock. It would also make the Attorney General the only one who can bring a civil case for a violation, require written notice first, and give the person 45 days to fix the problem. The act would take effect right away.

NJ-2026-A5733.title: Requires Office of Eviction Prevention to publish eviction-related data.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Housing Committee

NJ-2026-A5733.aiSummary: The bill would require the Office of Eviction Prevention to work with the state courts to collect eviction filing data by county and make it public on its website. The data would include counts of landlord-tenant cases, households served with court papers, eviction orders, evictions, and evictions avoided. It would take effect right away.

NJ-2026-A5729.title: Requires certain State agencies to establish expedited approval and permitting procedures for artificial intelligence data centers that bring their own power.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Science, Innovation and Technology Committee

NJ-2026-A5729.aiSummary: State agencies would have to set up faster approval and permit steps for artificial intelligence data centers that use power made on site from natural gas. The Board of Public Utilities, the Department of Community Affairs, and the Department of Environmental Protection would have to make these rules within 12 months after the law takes effect. The rules would also cover faster site review, building plan review, power hookup steps, and some environmental permits.

NJ-2026-A5724.title: Provides gross income tax credit for portion of employment-related dependent care expenses incurred by certain resident taxpayers.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Children, Families and Food Security Committee

NJ-2026-A5724.aiSummary: The bill would give certain New Jersey residents a state income tax credit for part of their work-related child care costs for a dependent under age 13. The credit would be limited to taxpayers with New Jersey taxable income of $300,000 or less, with rates that drop as income rises, and it could not be more than $5,000 per child each year. A taxpayer could not use the same expenses for both this credit and the existing state dependent care credit.

NJ-2026-A5715.title: Requires DVA to conduct study of Statewide Veterans Diversion Program.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Military and Veterans' Affairs Committee

NJ-2026-A5715.aiSummary: The bill would require the Department of Veterans Affairs, with the Attorney General, to study the Statewide Veterans Diversion Program. The study would look at treatment, case management, housing help, county practices, and program numbers for veterans and other eligible service members. The commissioner would then report the findings and any recommended changes within one year, and the act would take effect immediately.

NJ-2026-A5166.title: Prohibits municipalities from requiring certain plan approval related to addition of up to five van accessible parking spaces to existing parking facilities.

actions.text: Assembly Floor Amendment Passed (Quijano) (Voice)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Introduced, Referred to Assembly State and Local Government Committee

NJ-2026-A5166.aiSummary: Municipalities in New Jersey would not be able to require certain site plan approvals just for adding up to five van accessible parking spaces to an existing parking lot or parking structure in a commercial zone. These spaces must meet federal accessible parking standards, and the rule would apply unless the change cuts the number of parking spaces already required in the original plan. The bill would take effect right away.

NJ-2026-A3424.title: Grants priority course registration to certain student parents attending institutions of higher education.

actions.text: Assembly Floor Amendment Passed (Quijano) (Voice)
Reported out of Assembly Comm. with Amendments, 2nd Reading
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Higher Education Committee

NJ-2026-A3424.aiSummary: The bill would give priority course registration to certain student parents at colleges and other higher education schools. It would also require the Secretary of Higher Education to set rules and standards for checking who qualifies within six months after the bill becomes law. The bill would have to follow all federal and state rules on discrimination and privacy.

NJ-2026-A2772.title: Requires Division of Child Protection and Permanency to develop suicide screening and crisis response training for caseworkers.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (78-0-0)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Reported and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Children, Families and Food Security Committee

NJ-2026-A2772.aiSummary: The bill would require the Division of Child Protection and Permanency to create training on suicide screening and crisis response for caseworkers. The training would cover warning signs, how to respond if a child is at risk, and how to work with mental health workers, schools, resource parents, and community supports. It would be part of new caseworker training and ongoing training, and current caseworkers would have to complete it within 24 months of the bill taking effect.

NJ-2026-A1408.title: Broadens public awareness signage to include notices in Chinese and Korean.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (78-0-0)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Reported and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Judiciary Committee

NJ-2026-A1408.aiSummary: The bill would require certain businesses, public places, and transit sites to post human trafficking warning signs in English, Spanish, Chinese, and Korean. It would affect places like bars, airports, bus and rail stations, truck stops, hospitals, hotels, and some job and farm labor sites. A business that does not comply could face a $300 fine for a first offense and $1,000 for later offenses. The change would take effect immediately.
